title: Introduce layer catalog and fast-warm seed images for predictable CI caches
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Flaky cold CI times and unpredictable cache misses are causing long feedback loops for engineers (median cold build ~14m, P95 ~38m). Current approach relies on ad-hoc image priming and large monolithic 'builder' images that churn often, leading to low cache locality across repos and high network egress for layer fetches. Scope: implement an opinionated layer catalog and a 'fast-warm' seed image strategy that reduces cold startup variance and increases cache hit rate across pipelines. The feature includes: (1) a small catalog metadata service (read-only for CI) that maps common layer fingerprints to stable seed images; (2) periodic seed-image baker jobs that produce language/runtime-specific minimal images with pinned toolchain snapshots; (3) BuildKit configuration and GitHub Actions/Runner changes to prefer pulling from the seed image registry before remote fetching layers; (4) observability: dashboards to track seed image hit-rate, average pull size, and restore time; (5) signed seed images and daily vulnerability scans.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a layer catalog service with public read API used by CI workers
Bake and publish seed images for Go, Node, Python, and Rust containing pinned toolchains
Update BuildKit runner config to prioritize seed images and show >50% reduction in median cold CI time for targeted pipelines
Seed image hit rate >= 85% for supported languages in the week after rollout
Automated scanner runs on seed images with results surfaced in console and blocking on critical CVEs
comments: 2026-03-02 - Grooming notes: split work into service (ENG-555321-a), baker pipeline (ENG-555321-b), and runner rollout (ENG-555321-c). PM aligned on risk/release plan. Suggested estimate 5 points.

2026-03-05 - Prototype: built a minimal catalog prototype that returns a manifest for 'go:1.21-builder-minimal'. Cold build reduced from 14m -> 9m in micro-benchmarks. Prototype code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-prototypes/pull/87

2026-03-07 - Security flagged image signing and TTL requirements. Decided to use Cosign for signing and enforce 7-day rotation for ephemeral seed images; longer-lived canonical images for major language snapshots.

2026-03-09 - PR opened for baker job (infra/ci): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4213 — includes bake recipe for node/python/go/rust and a registry promotion step to gcr.redwood-inference.com/seed-images

2026-03-11 - Initial perf run on 'services/auth' pipeline shows cold median 14m -> 7.8m after seed pull. Noted one outlier due to missing buildkit cache mount config; created follow-up ENG-555322 to ensure runner mounts are standardized.

2026-03-12 - Design review (DX/Infra): opted for immutable layer naming (SHA256) + small manifest index to lookup language variants. Concerns raised about storage cost; PM accepted increased storage for 3x reduction in developer wait time.

2026-03-14 - Blocker: registry quota for signed manifests hit in prod region during canary. Reached out to cloud infra to request quota bump. Canary paused until 2026-03-16. Dashboard for metrics: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ci-buildcache?orgId=1&panelId=3
notes: Trade-offs: maintaining seed images increases ops surface area (scans, rotation), but significantly reduces wide-area layer fetches and improves reproducibility. We will monitor storage cost and add a TTL-based cleanup if costs exceed budget. Rollout plan: start with non-critical services -> platform services -> all pipelines with feature flag gating.
